name: git switch
shortDescription: Switch branches. Introduced in Git 2.23 as a safer, focused alternative to git checkout for branch operations only.
detailedDescription:
The `git switch` command was introduced in Git 2.23 (August 2019) to address the confusing dual nature of `git checkout`. While `git checkout` can both switch branches and restore files (two very different operations), `git switch` only handles branch switching.

This makes it safer — you can't accidentally destroy working directory changes by mistyping a command. It also has clearer error messages and more intuitive flag names (`-c` for create, instead of `-b`).

The command checks whether switching is safe (no conflicting uncommitted changes) before proceeding. If conflicts exist, it refuses and suggests committing, stashing, or using `--discard-changes`.

parameters.description: The branch to switch to. Must already exist locally or as a remote-tracking branch.
Create a new branch and switch to it. The clearer equivalent of `git checkout -b`.
Like -c, but if the branch already exists, reset it to the start point.
Switch to a commit in detached HEAD mode. Makes the intention explicit, unlike checkout where detached HEAD was a common accident.
Throw away any uncommitted local changes when switching. Equivalent to checkout's implicit behavior with --force.

examples.title: Switch to an existing branch
examples.code:
git switch main
git switch develop

examples.title: Create and switch to a new branch
examples.description: The -c flag is more memorable than checkout's -b.
examples.code:
git switch -c feature-notifications

# With a specific starting point:
git switch -c hotfix-auth origin/main

examples.title: Switch and discard local changes
examples.description: When you want to abandon current work and switch branches.
examples.code:
git switch --discard-changes main

# This destroys uncommitted changes — use with caution

examples.title: Track a remote branch automatically
examples.description: If a branch exists on the remote but not locally, git switch creates it automatically.
examples.code:
git fetch origin
git switch feature-api
# Automatically creates 'feature-api' tracking 'origin/feature-api'

commonMistakes.text: `git switch` is available from Git 2.23+. If you get 'git: switch is not a git command', update Git. On macOS: `brew upgrade git`. On Ubuntu: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:git-core/ppa && sudo apt update && sudo apt install git`.
`git switch` cannot restore files. For that, use `git restore`. This separation is intentional — it prevents the accidental data loss that was common with `git checkout`.
